metadata.title: feat: Add PLUGINS_CAN_OVERRIDE_AUTH_HEADERS feature flag for WXO auth
metadata.author: jonpspri

description:
## Summary
- Adds `PLUGINS_CAN_OVERRIDE_AUTH_HEADERS` setting (default `false`) to control whether pre-request plugin hooks can override auth-sensitive headers (`Authorization`, `Cookie`, `X-Api-Key`, `Proxy-Authorization`)
- Parameterizes `JWT_SECRET_KEY` across `docker-compose.yml` via env var substitution instead of hardcoded values
- Adds multi-tenant load test support with per-user JWT identity and `woTenantId` claims

## Test plan
- [x] Unit tests: deny-path (override blocked by default) and allow-path (override permitted when enabled)
- [x] All 27 tests in `test_http_auth_headers.py` pass
- [x] Black, isort, Bandit clean on changed files

comments.author: Copilot
comments.body: The environment variable documentation for `JWT_SECRET_KEY` still says the default is `my-test-key`, but the code now defaults to `my-test-key-but-now-longer-than-32-bytes`. Update the docstring so it matches the actual default (or reword to avoid hardcoding a specific default).

comments.author: Copilot
comments.body: Logging one INFO line per Locust user initialization (`User ... assigned to ...`) can produce very large log volume at higher user counts and skew load test results. Consider lowering this to DEBUG, logging only on a sample (e.g., first N users), or aggregating tenant assignment counts.

comments.author: Copilot
comments.body: This test relies on the global `settings.plugins_can_override_auth_headers` being `False`. If a developer runs tests with `PLUGINS_CAN_OVERRIDE_AUTH_HEADERS=true` in their environment (or another test mutates the settings object), this will fail. To make the test deterministic, explicitly patch/monkeypatch the middleware `settings` to `False` for the deny-path case as well.

comments.author: Copilot
comments.body: The new default JWT secret (`my-test-key-but-now-longer-than-32-bytes`) is still a fixed, well-known value, but it no longer matches the `weak_secrets` list in `mcpgateway/config.py` (which currently flags `my-test-key`). This reduces the effectiveness of the existing “default/weak secret” warning path; consider keeping the default as `my-test-key` (so warnings trigger) or adding the new default value to the weak-secret detection list / documentation as explicitly insecure dev-only.

comments.author: Copilot
comments.body: The auth-header override guard can be bypassed when a plugin uses different header casing (e.g. "Authorization"). `overridden` stores the original key strings, but the filter compares `k.lower()` against that set, so mixed-case keys won’t be stripped even when overrides are disabled. Normalize to lowercase when building `overridden` (and use that normalized set consistently) to ensure the guard reliably blocks overrides regardless of header key casing.

comments.author: Copilot
comments.body: This log line will raise `IndexError` at import time when `NUM_TENANTS` is set to 0 (or any value that results in an empty `TENANT_IDS`), because it indexes `[0]` and `[-1]`. Add validation (e.g., enforce `NUM_TENANTS >= 1`) or make the logging conditional when the list is empty.

## Pull request overview Adds a new gateway setting/feature flag to optionally allow trusted pre-request plugins (e.g., WXO auth) to override auth-sensitive inbound headers, and updates local/test infrastructure to support per-user JWT identities for multi-tenant load testing. **Changes:** - Introduces `PLUGINS_CAN_OVERRIDE_AUTH_HEADERS` (default `false`) and documents it. - Updates `HttpAuthMiddleware` to conditionally allow/deny plugin overrides of auth-protected headers. - Enhances the Locust echo-delay load test to generate per-user JWTs with `woTenantId` claims and adds `JWT_SECRET_KEY` env substitution across `docker-compose.yml`. ### Reviewed changes Copilot reviewed 7 out of 7 changed files in this pull request and generated 6 comments.
Show a summary per file | File | Description | | ---- | ----------- | | `mcpgateway/middleware/http_auth_middleware.py` | Gates auth-header override stripping behind the new settings flag. | | `mcpgateway/config.py` | Adds the `plugins_can_override_auth_headers` setting with security-focused description. | | `docs/docs/manage/configuration.md` | Documents the new gateway-level plugin security override setting. | | `docker-compose.yml` | Parameterizes `JWT_SECRET_KEY` and adds env wiring for the new flag and streamable HTTP tuning. | | `.env.example` | Adds example/commented config entry for `PLUGINS_CAN_OVERRIDE_AUTH_HEADERS`. | | `tests/unit/mcpgateway/middleware/test_http_auth_headers.py` | Adds unit tests for deny/allow behavior under the new flag. | | `tests/loadtest/locustfile_echo_delay.py` | Adds multi-tenant/per-user JWT generation for load testing. |
Comments suppressed due to low confidence (1) **mcpgateway/middleware/http_auth_middleware.py:149** * Merging `original_headers` and `modified_headers_dict` is currently case-sensitive, but the final scope header list lowercases names. If the original request had `authorization` and a plugin returns `Authorization`, `merged_headers` will contain both keys and you’ll emit duplicate `authorization` headers, leading to unpredictable auth behavior. Consider normalizing both dicts to lowercase keys before merging so there is exactly one value per logical header name. ``` merged_headers = {**original_headers, **modified_headers_dict} # Update request.scope["headers"] which is the raw header list Starlette uses # Convert dict to list of (name, value) tuples with lowercase byte keys request.scope["headers"] = [(name.lower().encode(), value.encode()) for name, value in merged_headers.items()] ```

reviews.author: crivetimihai
reviews.body:
## Review: LGTM — Approved

Rebased onto `main` and resolved 5 conflicted files. All 38 auth header tests and 758 utils tests pass.

### What this PR adds (after rebase onto main which already has the core feature)

- **Docker-compose**: Parameterizes `JWT_SECRET_KEY` via env var substitution across all services (was hardcoded `my-test-key`). Adds `PLUGINS_CAN_OVERRIDE_AUTH_HEADERS` and `STREAMABLE_HTTP_MAX_EVENTS_PER_STREAM` env vars.
- **Integration tests**: `TestPluginsCanOverrideAuthHeaders` (3 tests) — exercises the full middleware dispatch path, complementing the existing `TestRunPreRequestHooks` unit tests.
- **Documentation**: New "Gateway-Level Plugin Security Overrides" section in `configuration.md` with danger admonition. `.env.example` updated in both hot-toggles and detailed sections.
- **Load test resilience**: Auto-generation fallback when WXO auth is disabled, longer JWT secret default (32+ bytes to satisfy `min_secret_length`).
- **Test isolation**: New `conftest.py` for `tests/unit/mcpgateway/utils/` to prevent host env leakage into passthrough-header tests.

### Conflict resolution decisions

- Kept `--admin` flag on all JWT commands that had it on `main`
- Kept `main`'s explicit `ValueError` for `NUM_TENANTS < 1` (clearer than silent clamping)
- Kept `main`'s `run_pre_request_hooks()` refactored architecture (PR's inline auth protection was already integrated on `main`)
- Kept both `TestRunPreRequestHooks` (main) and `TestPluginsCanOverrideAuthHeaders` (PR) test classes

### Security

- Default-deny: correct (`plugins_can_override_auth_headers=False`)
- Protected headers: `{authorization, cookie, x-api-key, proxy-authorization}` — comprehensive
- Case-insensitive comparison prevents bypass via casing
- No bypass vectors identified

commits.message:
feat: Add PLUGINS_CAN_OVERRIDE_AUTH_HEADERS feature flag for WXO auth

Add a gateway-level setting (default false) that controls whether
pre-request plugin hooks can override auth-sensitive headers
(Authorization, Cookie, X-Api-Key, Proxy-Authorization). Required for
plugin-driven token exchange workflows such as WXO auth.

Changes:
- Add plugins_can_override_auth_headers to Settings with security docs
- Gate auth-header stripping in HttpAuthMiddleware behind the new flag
- Normalize plugin header keys to lowercase before merging to prevent
  duplicate scope entries from case mismatches
- Parameterize JWT_SECRET_KEY across docker-compose.yml via env var
  substitution instead of hardcoded values
- Add multi-tenant load test support with per-user JWT identity and
  woTenantId claims, with auto-generation fallback when WXO auth is
  disabled
- Add conftest to isolate passthrough header settings in utils tests
- Add unit tests for deny-path, allow-path, and case-sensitivity bypass

Signed-off-by: Jonathan Springer <jps@s390x.com>
commits.author: Jonathan Springer

commits.message:
fix(loadtest): add jti claim to auto-generated JWT tokens

The _generate_jwt_token() fallback in the load test was producing
tokens without a jti claim, which are rejected when REQUIRE_JTI=true
(the default). Add uuid-based jti to match what create_jwt_token CLI
produces.

Signed-off-by: Mihai Criveti <crivetimihai@gmail.com>
